lines: Registro: cotidiano gentil; cuidadora.
Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Registro: enigmático, profético, frio.
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.
Nosuri — `voice_criticality: medium`. Fora-da-lei atrevida e malandra; "aliada da justiça" irônica; oportunista. Registro coloquial/esperto.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Ougi — `voice_criticality: low`. Irmão da Nosuri; pragmático, parceria com a irmã.
Registro: confuso, desorientado, semi-consciente.
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Rulutieh — `voice_criticality: medium`. Princesa tímida e gentil; hesitante (gagueja quando nervosa: "P-Princesa..."), educada, se anima ao falar de arte/BL. Não soar arrogante apesar de princesa.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Anomalia 0x33f9 — texto PT/EN corrompido na fonte
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar a linha `0x33f9` como anomalia de fonte (não traduzir em cima do lixo; tratar como linha de sistema reescrita). **Razão:** A string original já vem misturada PT/EN e truncada ("...SISTEMAS AM . RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. lines.source: Eep...!
Amazing...
Hee hee. Makes my ears tickle, all this noise.
I wasn't expecting the hero's welcome...
I'm not very good with these situations.\n
It's a little embarrassing...
Their supply lines and communications were\n
totally cut off. They were desperate for this.
Guess that makes us big damn heroes.\n
Not really my thing, to be honest.
Still, a welcome like this makes that grueling\n
trip over the ocean all worth it.
Haku. I'll accompany Miss Nekone and see to\n
necessary protocols.
Thanks.
Kiwru, let's go get all this stuff unpacked\n
from the carts.
Oh, right!
Guess I'll stay here and keep an eye on the\n
supplies then.
I can't feel the usual vigor from the Yamatan\n
soldiers. Morale must be rock-bottom, going by\n
the mood.
Lord Haku.
I look up toward the source of the voice calling\n
my name.
Ah, Munechika.
On behalf of everyone here, I'd like to extend\n
formal thanks to you. You arrived just in time.
Don't worry about it. I'm just here in Tuskur to\n
try its cuisine. The delivery is a side gig.
Hmhm... It's reassuring to hear your nonchalance\n
again, Lord Haku.
Hm. I didn't notice it before, but Munechika...\n
seems pretty worn down, even if she is smiling.
I doubt she'll say as much openly, but the\n
battles up until now must have been\n
hard-fought.
You've nothing to worry yourself over. Thanks\n
to these provisions, the tide will turn in our\n
favor.
...I guess I was letting my expressions betray\n
my thoughts.
Oh, right. This is for you. Probably should\n
have led with it, but it's a letter from\n
Oshtor.
I see. It seems my debts to Lord Oshtor continue\n
to accumulate...
I doubt he sees it like that.
You're likely right, but even so, I won't soon\n
forget all the help he's given me.
That goes for you as well, Lord Haku.
Such a sense of obligation... But I guess that's\n
just how Munechika is.
Now, this letter transfers you to my command\n
as long as you're here. Is that correct?
Hm? Yeah.
Then I bid you follow me. I wish for you to\n
accompany me somewhere.
Munechika leads me to a tent much larger than\n
any of the others in the vicinity.
Along the way, she explains the current state\n
of the war.
You've doubtlessly noticed that conditions\n
are not favorable for us.
We've established a foothold in the area, but\n
thus far, we've been unable to progress any\n
further.
We've yet to meet them in a full-on battle,\n
but skirmishes arise at all times of the day\n
or night.
They appear as if from nowhere, raise a\n
commotion, then vanish beyond the treeline.
Any hunting parties we send out are unable to\n
track them down.
Many a squad has chased them too far out,\n
only to fall into a trap.
And so our numbers continue to slowly diminish,\n
while Tuskur's assaults persist relentlessly.
Fatigue is the single largest threat to our\n
campaign, now. The troops are wearing\n
themselves out.
Guess the home-turf advantage is a bigger factor\n
than I thought.
It's likely their knowledge of local, smaller\n
paths is enabling their guerilla tactics, yes.
Doubtlessly, they use those paths to stage\n
strikes on our supply lines, as well. We're\n
cut off.
I see. So it's possible they meant for you to\n
camp here all along? The area they know best?
Quite. The Tuskur general is well-versed in the\n
arts of war.
I've heard tell that Tuskur fought a large-scale\n
civil war some years ago... Perhaps that's why.
I remember my brother saying something to that\n
effect...
How he tried to negotiate a way to study this\n
land with the kamunagi, and how they denied him.
Maybe they've been anticipating Yamato resorting\n
to force all this time. They've been ready for\n
us.
Hm?
Munechika's beckoning pulls me out of my\n
thoughts as we arrive in front of the tent.
This is our forward command center. Please,\n
come in.
You are LATE, Munechika!
Apologies. I was seeing to the resupply and\n
reinforcement effort.
Oh? Then you must be part of the reinforcements.\n
Your name was... Haku? Forgive me, it's been\n
a while.
Yes. Lord Haku will be under my command for the\n
duration, so it is my wish that he joins our\n
meeting.
...I have no qualms. He may do as he likes.
Pffeh.
Raiko looks me over, and the corners of his\n
mouth turn up in a small grin.
Dekopompo, on the other hand, shoots me a\n
dubious glance as I follow Munechika to her\n
place.
I THOUGHT you looked familiar. Oshtor's lackey,\n
hm? You certainly ran your mouth at the war\n
council.
In my magnanimousness, I will forgive your\n
impertinence ONCE. I expect you to hold your\n
tongue.
Man, he REALLY doesn't like me, does he?\n
I guess it's because I'm more a mercenary than\n
a soldier...
Let's begin, if that's everything. Time is a\n
valuable resource. We oughtn't waste what we\n
have.
Indeed.
Dekopompo and the others seat themselves,\n
followed by Munechika. When I try to sit,\n
however--
Eh? O, joyous day! Master Haku! Look upon me,\n
Master Haku, and see a visage wracked with\n
rejoicing!
Huh...?
I'd recognize that voice anywhere.
Maro? How've you been?
Ho ho! Behold me, as fighting-fit as thou dost\n
remember! Maroro remaineth a PARAGON of health.
O, but how our reunion gladdens me! Forsooth,\n
thy presence is worth a hundred men and more--
Dekopompo levels a glare at him, and Maroro\n
freezes, sinking silently back into his chair.
Oh, right. I totally forgot he was working as\n
Dekopompo's tactician.
Seems like he's having a rough go of it, as\n
usual. Not sure if I can say anything to help\n
right now.
Bah, wasting our precious time...\n
Bokoinante! Begin.
As you say, sir.
The man called Bokoinante spreads a large map\n
across the table, then points out a particular\n
location.
Scout reports indicate an enemy stronghold in\n
this mountainous region, here.
We can reasonably assume the enemy troops\n
waylaying our forces are deploying from it.
One side is a sheer cliff, and the approach\n
is... made troublesome by the extremely\n
difficult terrain.
The assembled generals and their tacticians\n
lapse into silence at Bokoinante's grim\n
description.
He used the word "troublesome" to glaze over\n
the challenge, but it seems all but\n
insurmountable.
Not to mention the enemy's prior knowledge of\n
the territory, the terrible terrain disadvantage...
We can't rely on our numbers in such narrow\n
spaces, but deploying with fewer troops won't\n
help, either.
Which means the optimal strategy is probably--
Bah! This backwater country has only been able\n
to resist us thus far through sheer dumb luck!
This feeble "stronghold" will fall in but moments\n
if we rally our full, combined strength, yes?
Dekopompo suddenly bursts out in enthusiasm.
Look at our enemy! They avoid a head-on fight,\n
continuing to nip at our heels with these\n
skirmishes!
They fear our military might! They are weak,\n
pathetic in the extreme!
We should rally for a proper, frontal assault\n
on th--
No. As one who prides herself on defensive\n
tactics, I disagree.
I propose we abandon this location and make a\n
tactical retreat.
Nyargh!?
Dekopompo, shocked, ceases his flailing at\n
Munechika's words. She continues, ignoring his\n
reaction.
Holding our current position will only see our\n
numbers continue to diminish. We cannot push\n
forward.
I submit that our priority should be to retreat,\n
regroup, and reorganize our available troops.
Wha--Wh--Wh--!?
Absolutely not!
We are here under DIRECT orders from the Mikado!\n
Have you already forgotten!?
You expect us to stand before the enemy, then\n
turn tail and run!? To accept such naked SHAME?
Tuskur is primarily composed of woods and\n
mountains, with little in the way of flatland.
That is why they equip themselves lightly and\n
favor guerilla tactics over traditional\n
rakusharai style.
Our army is composed of rakusharai accustomed\n
to fighting on plains. We have no advantage\n
here.
Positioned as we are, we cannot fight at even\n
a fraction of our full potential.
Their fundamental tactics differ too much from\n
ours. I bid you remember how much we've\n
struggled.
They target our weaknesses. They understand we\n
cannot hold out forever. Our supplies are\n
limited.
Knowing that, would you still force a fight and\n
sacrifice the lives of our soldiers for pride?
Are you saying we're STRUGGLING against such\n
a tiny country!?
We have come here to SUBJUGATE these degenerate\n
primitives, as is the Mikado's will.
We can hardly afford to shame ourselves in\n
front of our enemy and flee!
I am not saying we should run outright.\n
I merely propose we find a more easily-supplied\n
Th-That statement itself REEKS of cowardice!\n
Where is your fighting spirit?
Or do you intend to controvert the Mikado's\n
will!?
Munechika, who'd maintained a conversational\n
tone up to this point, abruptly stands up.
I cannot abide such slander. You will retract\n
those words, sir.
Nyoh? Have I hit a sore spot? To be sure,\n
I'm astounded so disloyal a woman was made\n
one of the Eight Pillar Generals!
Dekopompo... Watch yourself.
Wh--!? The gall! You would address me by name\n
alone?
General you may be, but a baseborn RAT hardly\n
compares to one such as me! You've allowed\n
your ego to--
Be silent.
Nyeh! You dare...?
Munechika glares at Dekopompo, her eyes full of\n
cold fire, while he glares back in a furious\n
sweat.
This isn't good. Munechika's hard to rile, but\n
I can tell invoking the Mikado filled her with\n
rage.
The tension continues to escalate, right to the\n
edge of swords being drawn--but then a low voice\n
speaks.

Oh...

Nyurgh...

By your side.

Tell the others to--

Yeeeaaah, I had a feeling you'd say something\n

Hee hee.
Ah heh.

Take back the stolen supplies...

Searching...

That, ah...

Ahahaha...

Haku...?

Konjac?

Haku...

Ouch!

With Munechika's help, I was able to obtain\n

Rulutieh and the twins seem to be decent hands\n

Hm hm hm...
Hup, hup, hup.

Uh?

Gah!?

Ah... ahaha...
Oh...

Yeah?

Is this...?

This stuff...

Ah, this is better...
Quite intriguing.
This sauce is unfamiliar to me...

Kuon...

Hm?

Lady Kuon?
